output:
### Slide 1: Q1 Launch — Construction Subcontractors (10-200 Employees)
- Objective: Launch Tallyroad in new segment and create first repeatable pipeline engine
- CRO ask: 400 SQLs + 80 customers on $180,000 — we tested it against capacity and math
- Our plan: $161,830 program, 209 committed SQLs, ~40 customers, within 210 sales capacity
- Speaker note: We want a credible launch we can hit and learn from, not a miss we explain in April.

### Slide 2: Reality Check — 400 / 80 Is Not Achievable
- Sales capacity: 3 AEs x 70 SQLs = **210 SQLs max**; 400 SQLs would leave 190 untouched
- Customer math: 80 customers at 20% SQL→won **requires** 400 SQLs — zero room for new-segment dip
- Budget math: credible B2B cost/SQL is ~$750 blended; 400 x $750 = ~$300,000, well over $180,000
- Search cap: only 1,100 clicks/mo available; even at 100% capture = just 44 SQLs in Q1
- Speaker note: We recommend resetting to 200-210 SQLs and 40 customers, or add budget and sales capacity.

### Slide 3: Funnel Math — Committed Plan
- Formulas: Spend = Clicks x CPC or fixed fee; Leads = Spend / CPL (Search: Clicks x 6% CVR); SQLs = Leads x Lead→SQL; Cost/SQL = Spend / SQLs
- | Channel | Spend | Leads | SQLs | Cost/SQL |
- | Paid Search | $16,830 | 198 | 44 | $383 |
- | LinkedIn Lead-Gen | $84,000 | 600 | 108 | $778 |
- | Content Syndication | $11,000 | 200 | 12 | $917 |
- | BuildExpo West | $45,000 | 300 | 45 | $1,000 |
- | **Total Committed** | **$156,830** | **1,298** | **209** | **$750** |
- Plus $5,000 Facebook test (417 leads, SQLs not forecasted) = $161,830 total, $18,170 under budget
- Speaker note: This is the max credible SQLs we can buy and work without relying on consumer-app Facebook numbers.

### Slide 4: Channel Mix & Budget Allocation ($161,830 of $180,000)
- Paid Search $16,830 (10%): Capture all high-intent job-costing + expense terms; capped by volume
- LinkedIn Lead-Gen $84,000 (52%): Core scale engine — GCs, subs, ops + finance titles, 10-200 size filter
- BuildExpo West $45,000 (28%): Feb 10-12 anchor for trust, demos, and 300 scans; expensive but high intent
- Content Syndication $11,000 (7%): Small test only — $917/SQL and 6% qualify rate is too wasteful to scale
- Facebook $5,000 (3%): Isolated test — $12 CPL is from a consumer app, do not plan on it
- Speaker note: We maxed the cheapest credible channel first, then scaled LinkedIn, and held $18k as reserve.

### Slide 5: Messaging Pillars — From 12 Interviews
- Pillar 1 — Every Receipt Tied to Every Job (10/12): Track materials receipts by job from the yard, no more shoeboxes
- Pillar 2 — Pay Field Crews Fast (8/12): Same-day reimbursement via mobile snap + approval by foreman
- Pillar 3 — QuickBooks Sync That Reconciles (7/12): Jobs, codes, and cards map cleanly, month-end in hours
- Proof for all: Subcontractor demo video, foreman phone UI, QuickBooks reconciliation screenshot
- Speaker note: We lead with job-costing receipts everywhere because that was nearly unanimous.

### Slide 6: Timeline — Built Around BuildExpo West (Feb 10-12)
- January — Build: Launch search + LinkedIn v1, ship construction landing pages, pre-book booth meetings, warm list
- Early Feb — Amplify: Pre-show LinkedIn + search surge, crew-reimbursement creative, scan-to-demo workflow test
- Feb 10-12 — Convert: BuildExpo live demos, 300-scan goal, same-day SDR follow-up, LinkedIn retarget attendees
- Late Feb-March — Harvest: 48-hour scan nurture, expand winning LinkedIn audiences, cut losers, shift reserve to scale
- Speaker note: Everything in January exists to make the booth convert, everything in March exists to close it.

### Slide 7: KPIs & Weekly Leading Indicators
- Lagging Q1 goals: 209 SQLs, 42 x 20% = ~40 customers, $384k ARR, ~$4,050 CAC, pipeline coverage
- Weekly funnel: Clicks vs 1,100/mo cap, CPC vs $5.10, landing CVR vs 6%, CPL by channel, Lead→SQL vs 22%/18%/6%/15%
- Sales health: % SQLs worked <24hrs, meetings held, SQL→won vs 20%, disqualify reasons by segment
- Action rule: Pause content syndication if Lead→SQL <5% for 2 weeks; move $ to LinkedIn/search retargeting
- Speaker note: We will know by week 3 if new-segment conversion is holding or if we need to reforecast customers.

### Slide 8: Risks — What Could Break This
- New-segment conversion risk: Professional-services rates may not transfer; plan assumes 22%/18% hold
- Concentration risk: 52% on LinkedIn + 28% on one show; CPC inflation or weak foot traffic hits Q1 hard
- Capacity risk: 209 SQLs uses 99% of AE time; no slack for Facebook upside or slow follow-up
- False-economy risk: Scaling $12 Facebook CPL or $55 syndication would hit lead goals but flood sales with junk
- Speaker note: Our biggest risk is pretending cheap leads equal pipeline, so we ring-fenced those tests.

### Slide 9: Decision Needed From Leadership
- Approve revised Q1 targets: **205-210 SQLs and 40 customers (stretch) / 32 at 16% close**, not 400 / 80
- Approve $161,830 mix + hold $18,170 reserve to double-down post-BuildExpo on winner
- Agree: Sales works max 210 SQLs with 24-hr SLA; excess goes to nurture, not AEs; no scale of Facebook without proof
- Speaker note: If you want 400/80, we need ~$300k+ and 3 more AEs — otherwise let us execute this focused launch.
